details: Bitcoin showed slight gains on Monday but remained in a narrow trading range. Heightened risk aversion stemming from the ongoing U.S.-Iran standoff in the Strait of Hormuz has suppressed investor appetite for speculative assets like cryptocurrencies, pushing up oil prices. Additionally, continued capital outflows from major spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and upcoming U.S. regulatory meetings involving top crypto leaders are contributing to subdued crypto market sentiment.
title: US-Iran Tensions & Regulations Impact Crypto Markets

details: The European Union has extended its transaction ban to 14 crypto-related service platforms operating from countries including Georgia, Panama, the UAE, the Marshall Islands, Kyrgyzstan, and Belarus. These measures are part of the EU's 21st package of restrictive actions against Russia, also introducing the potential for a complete third-country ban on crypto-asset services to prevent sanctions circumvention.
title: EU Implements Transaction Ban on Crypto Platforms

details: Global macroeconomic conditions reveal a mixed picture. While the past week saw a weakened case for an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase due to softer U.S. retail sales and consumer sentiment, inflation risks persist, partly due to elevated energy costs. Oil prices, in particular, remain a significant macroeconomic threat, with increases driven by tanker attacks, reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations. Despite these challenges, major stock indices like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq continued their weekly gains, though markets are becoming more selective.
title: Global Markets Face Inflation and Geopolitical Headwinds

details: On August 7, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on digital asset exchanges relied upon by the Iranian regime to launder billions of dollars and support the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and other terrorist groups. This action targets two major digital asset exchanges and a network of front companies facilitating illicit cryptocurrency activity and sanctions evasion, following Iran's attacks against commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Crypto Exchanges Funding Iranian IRGC
